raw_response:
I’m only farming 3 mu, so I can’t take big risks. Stevia is my cash crop, and what matters most for me is getting the stand established well, keeping the field clean early, and not spending too much cash at one time. I have well water, so if spring is dry I’ll irrigate after transplanting to help survival, but I won’t water too often because pumping costs money. The extension people say stevia responds to fertilizer, but on a small plot like mine I’d rather use a moderate rate and split it, because if I put it all at once and we get poor weather, that money is already buried in the ground. I’ll use improved seedlings if I can get them locally, do normal rotary tillage before planting, control weeds early, and then topdress after the plants are established. My goal is not the highest possible yield, it is a steady harvest and reliable cash income.
